weapon_types.name: Pistol
weapon_types.text:
Pistol weapons may:

- Make Shooting Attacks against enemy units within 3" at the models full Ballistic Skill (BS) characteristic.
- Make Shooting Attacks even if the equipped model Advanced.
- Make Shooting Attacks at full Ballistic Skill (BS) even if the equipped model Retreated or Fell Back. In addition, a model with a Pistol weapon can shoot in the Shooting phase and still declare a charge in the Charge Phase.

A Model armed with Pistols may shoot with up to two of them when declaring a shooting attack.

weapon_types.name: Rapid Fire
weapon_types.text: Rapid Fire weapons double the number of attacks they make if the target of the shooting attack is within half the range of the weapon. A model that fires a Rapid Fire weapon may not declare a charge in the Charge Phase.

weapon_types.name: Assault
weapon_types.text: A model equipped with an Assault Weapon may shoot in the Shooting Phase and still declare a charge in the Charge Phase.

weapon_types.name: Heavy
weapon_types.text: If a model with a Heavy Weapon moves in the Movement phase (see 6.1), shooting attacks with the Heavy weapon are made as Snap Shots. A unit with a model that makes a shooting attack with a Heavy Weapon in the shooting phase may not declare a charge in the Charge Phase.

weapon_types.name: Grenade
weapon_types.text: Only 1 model in a unit can make a shooting attack with a Grenade weapon. In addition, a model with a Grenade weapon can shoot in the Shooting phase and still declare a charge in the Charge Phase. Grenade weapons may be used as melee weapons in the Combat Phase but only when targeting Vehicle, Fortification or Aircraft type units. However, only 1 model in the unit can make an attack with the Grenade weapon. Grenade weapons used in melee do not use the Blast or Large Blast special rule.

weapon_types.name: Melee
weapon_types.note: The core rules define no Melee weapon type. §12.2 and §12.2.1 use the term.
